fields.value: Saturate the GPU in shared eval serving

Jack Heart (2026-11-15): "ok thatw enough to confirm the direction and proceed and then add a task for trying to saturate the gpu".

Problem: after EXP-73 (#117), one agent process per machine batches checkpoint forwards for separate game processes. On a 4090 with the frozen Manabot 256-game panel it plays 8,131-9,933 games/hour, 1.02-1.06x Manabot's own server, with identical trajectories. The GPU stays about 29% busy as rows per forward rise from 20 to 35 (32 to 64 games at a time), so the limit is on the host, not the GPU. Evidence: EXP-73 checkout scratch/protocol/fair-comparison.txt and fair-1-evidence/; history in scratch/exp-73-group-an-experiment.md; survey in EXP-66 scratch/shared-inference-survey.md.

Outcome: large-checkpoint GPU eval throughput rises well past the #117 baseline, toward a busy GPU, without changing the author API (Agents(load=, build=), play(match, agents)) or the identical-trajectory guarantee.

Start by attributing agent-process host time per forward (input stacking, transfer, sampling, replies, queue wait) and one cell above 64 games at a time. Candidates, chosen by measurement: overlap preparing the next batch with the current forward (pinned buffers, CUDA streams), several batchers or agent processes per GPU, larger concurrency, and filling freed slots across grouped eval jobs to shorten the 21-24 s tail. Priorities (loose, Jack Heart): large-model GPU perf, then client API simplicity, then small CPU perf, then prior art.

Constraints: AGENTS.md; each measurement round at most 30 minutes of rental; ask for a dollar allowance before renting. Starts after #117 lands. No release.
